problems.severity: medium blocker, this card's own test file, introduced by the round-2 fix
problems.title: W0301-FRESH-OBSERVATION-UNLOCKS carries a hard-coded timestamp and deterministically FAILS from 2026-10-02T00:00:01Z UTC onward
problems.detail: tests/domain/check/main.go:340 runs EnsureClientSessionFence, which seeds the (pf,run-f) barrier with restored_at = domain.Now() (wall clock, RFC3339Nano); line 346's INSERT OR IGNORE of the fixed '2026-10-01T00:00:00Z' can never lower it; line 352-356 then inserts the unlock observation with the literal observed_at '2026-10-02T00:00:00Z' and requires the epoch advance to succeed. Today that holds (my three runs). Once the UTC clock passes 2026-10-02T00:00:01Z, restored_at > observed_at for every future run, the trigger aborts, and the assertion - and with it the entire bound command, exit 1 - fails forever. I reproduced the exact mechanism: with restored_at forced to '2026-10-02T00:00:01Z' the same production-shape observation is refused (probe B21), while with restored_at pinned to '2026-10-01T00:00:00Z' the same literal unlocks (control B21b). The product code is correct; only the test is time-bombed, but the test IS the card's acceptance harness, and the loop reruns it (dispatcher gates, W03-99 parent-gate regressions, any future re-verification).
problems.fix: make the observation timestamp derived rather than a fixed future literal: either insert observed_at = domain.Now() at that point in the sequence (like W0301-OBSERV-INSERT's siblings should have been), or pin restored_at deterministically - e.g. after EnsureClientSessionFence, UPDATE backup_restore_barriers SET restored_at='2026-10-01T00:00:00Z' and keep the fixed future observation - so the assertion passes on every clock. One line, re-run the 47.

summary: Round-2 rework is substantively real: I verified with my own probes on real migrated databases that the three contract timestamps now land as RFC3339Nano Z-strings consistent with created_at (including sealed_at through the MapClientSession path the shipped check still omits); that the fresh-observation fence dropped its unsatisfiable epoch-equality, demands the same children_stopped+queue_empty evidence as the Run fence, unlocks a writer_epoch-3 session via domain.HandoffEpoch on an observation carrying the run's lease_epoch 7, skips SETTLED runs entirely (no barrier, free handoff), lets run-less sessions advance while still aborting regressions, and re-blocks after a second restore; that ErrUnknownSession/ErrStaleWatermark/ErrSealed are cleanly separated with no sql.ErrNoRows leakage; that the CRLF incident is fully reversed (the only round-2 change to backup_recovery.go is byte-exact CR removal, +3/0 against the pre-card baseline, 5 files at 0 CR bytes); that the redundant open-index is gone, writer_client_id carries a SQL length CHECK and two open sessions coexist; and that commands.json rev5 registers the fence file with hash 3f5f5b1b matching both the archived and my fresh dispatcher runs (PASS 47, exit 0, at 3225a31f; W03-99/W03-02 exit 3). The glob scoping fix addresses a real self-inflicted break (21 *.sql at the production root vs required 13/14/20), and the three named legacy tests pass. The disclosed pre-existing failures check out for TestW17UpgradeActiveRecovery (identical line-699 runtime_dispatches error reproduced in my detached 6eacb1cb worktree, since removed) but the receipt overstates the second test's baseline evidence - it is a genuine pre-existing flake (fails intermittently at baseline AND HEAD, never with runtime_dispatches), so only the wording is wrong, not the conclusion. What stops ACCEPTED this time is a single new test-side landmine: the unlock assertion pins observed_at to '2026-10-02T00:00:00Z' while the fence stamps restored_at from the wall clock, which I showed blocks the very update the assertion demands once the clock passes 2026-10-02T00:00:01Z UTC - i.e. tonight. Fix that one line, correct the disclosure text, and this card's evidence will finally be re-runnable.
